newsitem.title: JAPAN: S.Korea to remain open-spec naphtha buyer-traders.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea to remain open-spec naphtha buyer-traders.

text.p: South Korean firms withdrew a proposal to convert their status in open-spec naphtha trading from a buyer to cargo supplier on the second day of an annual naphtha conference in Tokyo, participants said on Tuesday.
"They (South Korean firms) withdrew the request this morning at the conference after discussing the matter among themselves," one participant of the two-day meeting said.
Open-spec naphtha is currently traded on a C and F (cost and freight) Japan or South Korea basis, restricting the two east Asian countries to buyers of open-spec cargoes.

However, some oil firms in South Korea were aiming to take part in the Asian benchmark forward contract trading as cargo suppliers rather than buyers as the country's refining capacity grows, traders said.
South Korean companies were probably unable to reach a unanimous agreement on the matter due to objections from South Korean petrochemical firms, some traders said.
A possible simplification to quality standards for open-spec cargoes was also discussed at the meeting, naphtha traders said.
Currently, cargoes with different origins have to meet different sets of quality standards to be traded in the open-spec naphtha chain, making paper work complicated.
Selected panelists for the conference are expected to come up with a draft proposal on simplifying standards later this year, the traders said.
